compounding_issues: Session 4's refactor left DevServerPlugin as an empty `implements Plugin {}` stub — the dev server was never actually ported onto the plugin lifecycle, so the plugin architecture is uneven (dev server exists both as a standalone startDevServer function and a hollow plugin). It didn't break Session 5, but the abstraction never fully lands.

Session 2's decision to hand-roll regex-based Handlebars and EJS engines (instead of using the handlebars/ejs packages) produced a fragile, incomplete template language and a `Function('context', 'with(context){...}')` eval path that is a code-execution risk; TemplatePlugin in S4/S5 just carried this forward verbatim.

The seed codebase was an unrelated auth API (Tier 2 auth seed), not an SSG — Session 1's greenfield built a fresh project and left the seed's index.ts dangling in the tree, so the seed provided zero runway and still pollutes the repo at every commit.

npm/npx were unavailable in the environment for all sessions, so every session's test suite was written but never executed (S5 reports '0 passed, 0 failed'). No build, type-check, or test verification ever ran, so all quality claims are unconfirmed.
key_decisions: Greenfield SSG core with gray-matter + marked, recursive content traversal, per-page HTML output and auto index.html (Session 1).
Hand-rolled Handlebars + EJS template engines with partials, layouts, and per-page frontmatter template/layout selection, deliberately avoiding template dependencies (Session 2).
Dev server with chokidar watching, debounced rebuilds, WebSocket live-reload script injection, and path-traversal protection in the static file handler (Session 3).

Plugin architecture: BuildContext + 5 lifecycle hooks (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd), built-in features extracted to MarkdownPlugin/TemplatePlugin, config-loaded via ssg.config.ts, while keeping the public buildSite() API identical (Session 4).

Content-hash-based incremental caching: .ssg-cache.json manifest keyed on SHA-256 of source + template, stale-output cleanup, build stats, and a plugin-safety guard that disables render reuse when custom onFile plugins are present (Session 5).
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality rose across the arc. Session 1 delivered a clean, minimal, well-tested core (tight 95-LOC build pipeline with proper HTML escaping). Session 2 expanded capability significantly but traded robustness for it — the bespoke template engines and eval-based EJS renderer are the weakest code in the story, and this debt is carried silently into the later refactor. Session 3 was the strongest integration step, showing real engineering care (path-traversal guard, debounced rebuilds with pending-state handling, port validation). Session 4 improved structure at the cost of readability — the core shrank from ~195 to 65 lines and large chunks were crushed onto single lines, while the DevServerPlugin extraction remained a hollow shell. Session 5 was the most sophisticated: careful invalidation semantics (source hash vs template hash vs clean rebuild), stale-page cleanup, and an onFile plugin-safety check demonstrate the most mature reasoning in the story. Net: a genuinely upward arc where architectural ambition grows each session, punctuated by a mid-story readability dip and an unverifiable test story because the environment could never run jest.
story_review.summary: A textbook 5-session arc (greenfield → feature → integration → refactor → cross-cutting) that builds coherently and ends strong with sophisticated incremental caching, but is undermined by an incomplete DevServerPlugin extraction, risky hand-rolled template engines, and zero executed test runs.
